common.applies_to: Established bush rose (Hybrid Tea, Floribunda, provisional Grandiflora); dormant pruning
common.preserved_uncertainty: Most sources don't treat an inward-growing stem as its own defect; they prevent it by cutting to an outward-facing bud (IG AF-1, Moderate). Only a few name it as something to find and remove, and their standard is a soft judgement ("not growing in a graceful, natural direction"). A stem curving toward a gap in the light could be mistaken for inward growth. That's a plausible but unsourced caution, worth bearing in mind, not a rule (IG §6 default). No beginner lookalike list exists (IG §6).

content.look_for: Now let's look for stems growing into the centre of the bush.

criteria.text: A stem growing toward the centre of the bush is a candidate. No source gives a more specific sign.

content.photo_limit: One photo has real limits for judging which way a stem grows. Look from more than one side.
content.confirm_question: Check the stem on your rose from more than one side. Is it growing into the centre?
content.not_sure_guidance: Take another photo that shows the middle of the bush more clearly, and look again from another side.
content.any_more_question: Can you see any more stems growing inward?
